## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the H(curl), H(div), and real $L^2$ inner-product interfaces used here; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching tetrahedral mesh with realization $|\mathcal T|=\overline\Omega$. Define $C_k(\mathcal T;\mathbb R)$ by extending the oriented chain groups of [[def-oriented-simplicial-cell-chains]] to real coefficients, and put $C^k=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(C_k,\mathbb R)$ with coboundary $\delta^k=\partial_{k+1}^*$. The degrees of freedom give a cochain isomorphism from
$$W_h^0\xrightarrow{\nabla}N_h^1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{curl}}N_h^2\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}N_h^3$$
to $C^0\xrightarrow{\delta^0}C^1\xrightarrow{\delta^1}C^2\xrightarrow{\delta^2}C^3$. Consequently the discrete cohomology in degree $k$ is naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R),\mathbb R)$. If $\overline\Omega$ is nonempty, connected, and contractible, then the sequence is exact at every positive-degree space, $\ker\nabla$ consists of constants, and $\operatorname{div}:N_h^2\to N_h^3$ is onto. For general topology, define
$$\mathcal H_h^1:=\ker(\operatorname{curl}|_{N_h^1})\cap(\nabla W_h^0)^\perp,\qquad \mathcal H_h^2:=\ker(\operatorname{div}|_{N_h^2})\cap(\operatorname{curl}N_h^1)^\perp$$
using the $L^2$ inner product. Then $\ker\operatorname{curl}=\nabla W_h^0\oplus\mathcal H_h^1$ and $\ker\operatorname{div}=\operatorname{curl}N_h^1\oplus\mathcal H_h^2$, with $\dim\mathcal H_h^k=\dim H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R)$ for $k=1,2$.

1.1 If $\mathcal T=\varnothing$, [F12] gives $\Omega=\varnothing$; by [F1] and [F4] all real chain, cochain, and finite-element spaces are zero, and [F11] gives $H_k(\varnothing;\mathbb R)=0$. All cohomology and harmonic statements then reduce to the unique maps and decompositions of zero spaces, and the nonempty contractible branch is inapplicable. Suppose henceforth that $\mathcal T\ne\varnothing$. In degree zero, the vertex basis $\lambda_i$ is dual to vertex evaluation; a value at each vertex determines a unique affine function on each incident tetrahedron, and common-face traces agree because they agree at the face vertices. Thus $J^0:W_h^0\to C^0$ is a bijection. In degree one, [F2] makes the six local edge moments a bijection between each local Nedelec space and its six edge values. The definition of $N_h^1$ imposes one value for each globally oriented edge. Any global assignment therefore determines the unique local fields on each cell, and [F3] makes their assembly a global H(curl) field; conversely, zero global moments force every cell restriction to vanish by [F2]. Thus $J^1:N_h^1\to C^1$ is a bijection. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F11, F12, given, construct]

2.1 In degree two, the four oriented face fluxes determine each local $RT_0$ field by [F3]. The definition of $N_h^2$ imposes one value for every global oriented face; these values determine unique local fields and [F3] assembles them into a global H(div) field. Zero global fluxes force every local field to vanish, so $J^2:N_h^2\to C^2$ is a bijection. In degree three, a constant is determined by its cell integral, so $J^3:N_h^3\to C^3$ is a bijection. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The dual differential $\delta^k$ evaluates a cochain on the oriented boundary of each $(k+1)$-simplex. For $k=0$, its value on an oriented edge is the terminal nodal value minus the initial value; for $k=1$, its value on a face is the signed sum of its boundary-edge circulations; and for $k=2$, its value on a tetrahedron is the signed sum of its boundary-face fluxes. By [F3] these are exactly the degrees of freedom of $\nabla$, $\operatorname{curl}$, and $\operatorname{div}$. Thus $J^{k+1}d_h=\delta^kJ^k$ for each differential. By [F8], $\delta^{k+1}\delta^k=0$, so these maps are cochain complexes and the bijections induce isomorphisms on cohomology. [A1, F3, F4, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Write $Z_k=\ker\partial_k$ and $B_k=\operatorname{im}\partial_{k+1}$; [F8] gives $B_k\subseteq Z_k$. Identify each cochain with its coordinate functional on the oriented simplex basis. Then $\ker\delta^k$ consists exactly of functionals vanishing on $B_k$, namely $B_k^\perp$. The image of $\delta^{k-1}=\partial_k^*$ lies in $Z_k^\perp$, since $(\partial_k^*\ell)(z)=\ell(\partial_kz)=0$ for $z\in Z_k$. These two subspaces have the same dimension: $\dim\operatorname{im}\partial_k^*=\operatorname{rank}\partial_k=\dim C_k-\dim Z_k=\dim Z_k^\perp$, so $\operatorname{im}\partial_k^*=Z_k^\perp$. Restricting a functional in $B_k^\perp$ to $Z_k$ therefore descends to $Z_k/B_k$ and has kernel $Z_k^\perp$. Every functional on $Z_k/B_k$ pulls back to a functional on $Z_k$ vanishing on $B_k$; extend a finite basis of $Z_k$ to one of $C_k$ and set the added basis values to zero. This proves surjectivity of restriction and hence $H^k(C^*)=B_k^\perp/Z_k^\perp\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(Z_k/B_k,\mathbb R)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb R}(H_k^{\mathrm{simp}}(\mathcal T;\mathbb R),\mathbb R)$. Since these spaces are finite dimensional, their real duals have the same dimension. [F4, F8, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By [F5], $H_k^{\mathrm{simp}}(\mathcal T;\mathbb R)\cong H_k(|\mathcal T|;\mathbb R)$. If $|\mathcal T|=\overline\Omega$ is nonempty, connected, and contractible in the sense of [F7], [F6] makes this group $\mathbb R$ for $k=0$ and zero for $k>0$. Steps 1.1–2.2 therefore show that the discrete cohomology is one-dimensional in degree zero and zero in positive degrees, which is exactness of the displayed finite sequence, including surjectivity of its last map. The globally constant functions lie in $W_h^0$ and have zero gradient, so the one-dimensional degree-zero kernel consists exactly of constants. [A1, F1, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 For arbitrary topology, let $Z_h^1=\ker\operatorname{curl}$ and $B_h^1=\nabla W_h^0$. By step 3.1, $B_h^1\subseteq Z_h^1$. The space $Z_h^1$ is finite dimensional as a subspace of $N_h^1$, so [F10] applied inside $Z_h^1$ gives $Z_h^1=B_h^1\oplus(Z_h^1\cap(B_h^1)^\perp)$ with orthogonality from [F9]. to $C^0\xrightarrow{\delta^0}C^1\xrightarrow{\delta^1}C^2\xrightarrow{\delta^2}C^3$. abla)v\cdot w$. Thus $|c(w;v,w)|\le\|

## Example

Assume Countable Choice. For any admissible overlap radius $\delta$ in the
structured family of
[[thm-two-level-p1-poisson-stable-decomposition]], put $r=H/\delta$.
Substitution into the proved stable-decomposition guarantee gives
$$ C_0\le C_{\rm FE}(1+r^2). $$
Along admissible families with $\delta/H\to0$, this upper-bound formula grows.
This substitution does not assert that the actual stable constant or
condition number must diverge.
1.1 Put $r=H/\delta$. Substituting into [F1] gives $C_0\le C_{\rm FE}(1+r^2)$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 To exhibit admissible radii with $\delta/H\to0$, fix $M,d$, put $a=1/M$, choose $q_0=\lceil\sqrt d\rceil$, and take $\delta=q_0a/n$ as $n\to\infty$ with $n\ge q_0$. Then $h=\sqrt d\,a/n\le\delta\le a$, and $r=H/\delta=\sqrt d\,n/q_0\to\infty$. The right side of the one-sided upper-bound formula grows; it supplies no lower estimate on the actual stable constant or condition number. [step 1.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For the system of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], U={z:ρ_i(q)>0 for every i} is open and its finite-dimensional vector field F is continuous and locally Lipschitz on U. From each initial state z₀∈U there is a unique local C¹ solution.

1.1 Each ρ_i is continuous by [F1], so U is open as the finite intersection of the inverse images of (0,∞). On U, denominators ρ_i² are nonzero, P is C¹, W_ε is C², and the finite sums defining F are continuous. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Fix z₀∈U. Since U is open, choose a nonempty nondegenerate closed box K about z₀ small enough to lie in U. It is convex and compact by [F4]. Each ρ_i is continuous and positive on K, so [F4] gives a positive minimum for each; taking the minimum over finitely many i gives a positive lower density bound on K. [F2] makes F Lipschitz there. Regard F as time-independent on R×U and apply [F3] to obtain a unique local C¹ solution. No choice principle is used. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain and
$\mathcal T_h$ any finite matching shape-regular simplicial mesh. There is a
constant $C$ depending only on $\Omega$, $d$, and the shape-regularity bound
such that every $v_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$ satisfies
$$\|v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
1.1 Apply [F2] to $E_hv_h\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ and use [F1] to obtain $\|E_hv_h\|_2\le(b-a)\|\nabla E_hv_h\|_2\le C(b-a)\|\nabla_hv_h\|_2$. [A1, F1, F2, given]

2.1 By the triangle inequality and [F1], $\|v_h\|_2\le\|v_h-E_hv_h\|_2+\|E_hv_h\|_2 \le Ch\|\nabla_hv_h\|_2+C(b-a)\|\nabla_hv_h\|_2.$ The mesh cells lie in the bounded domain, so $h\le\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)$; absorb this fixed bound into $C$. [A1, F1, step 1.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the mesh, coefficient, penalty, and exact-solution hypotheses of [[thm-sipdg-exact-consistency]] and [[thm-sipdg-coercivity-large-penalty]]. Let $u_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$ be the unique discrete solution, so $a_h(u_h,v_h)=\ell_h(v_h)$ for every $v_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$. Let $C_{\rm flux}$ be the constant in [[lem-sipdg-discrete-flux-inverse-bound]] and put $C_B:=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}$. Then for every $w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}$,
$$\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\bigl(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\bigr)\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}.$$
Consequently $\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\bigl(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\bigr)\inf_{w_h\in V_h^{\rm br}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$. The augmented approximation term retains the face-flux trace needed to bound the SIP consistency terms; no approximation rate is asserted without a separate bound on that term.

1.1 The exact solution $u$ is cellwise $H^2$ and $u_h,w_h$ are broken polynomials, so $u-w_h$ and $u_h-w_h$ belong to $\mathcal D_h$. The boundedness constant for their form pairing is $C_B=2+2\gamma^{-1/2}$ by [F5]. [F1, F5, given]

2.1 Fix $w_h$ and set $z_h=u_h-w_h$. If $z_h=0$ the estimate for this choice is immediate. Otherwise, coercivity [F2], the discrete equation and exact consistency [F3] give $\tfrac12\|z_h\|_{DG}^2\le a_h(z_h,z_h)=a_h(u-w_h,z_h)$. By [F4] and $\sum_K\int_K\nabla z_h^TA_K\nabla z_h\le\|z_h\|_{DG}^2$, $\|z_h\|_{DG,*}\le\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|z_h\|_{DG}$. Apply [F5] and step 1.1 to obtain $\tfrac12\|z_h\|_{DG}^2\le C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}\|z_h\|_{DG}$. Dividing by $\|z_h\|_{DG}>0$ proves $\|z_h\|_{DG}\le2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}}\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Since $\|\cdot\|_{DG}$ is a seminorm on $\mathcal D_h$ by [F5], its triangle inequality and step 2.1 give $\|u-u_h\|_{DG}\le\|u-w_h\|_{DG}+\|w_h-u_h\|_{DG}\le(1+2C_B\sqrt{1+C_{\rm flux}})\|u-w_h\|_{DG,*}$. This holds for every $w_h$, so taking the infimum proves both assertions. [F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For finite exact dyadic data and finite encoded controls, the procedure
[[alg-nufft-certified-gaussian-gridding-type1-type2]] terminates with a defined
status. Malformed global controls or structurally invalid candidates return
`invalid-input` as specified. On admissible controls, the empty-source branch
returns its exact zero or empty output; otherwise the procedure returns the
first candidate whose complete finite outward bound meets the exact positive
requested tolerance with status `certified`, or returns `inconclusive` with
the first recorded non-success reason in candidate order after the finite
list is exhausted. This includes `requested-tolerance-not-met` when all
candidates have finite valid bounds exceeding the requested tolerance.

Every performed interval division has its prescribed nonzero divisor guard,
FFT inputs and twiddle certificates pass the declared checks before use, and
every returned finite interval contains the exact value of its evaluated
DAG. A candidate with a range failure or unresolved interval, denominator, phase, FFT,
radius or tolerance check is not itself returned as certified; a later candidate
may still succeed. These are termination
and well-defined-status assertions for the specified procedure; its complete
transform-error estimates are separate mathematical claims.

1.1 The elementary evaluator in [F2] visits a finite typed DAG in topological order. Its series have the fixed finite index $J$; its exponential scaling uses a finite integer number of squarings; logarithm bins are a finite integer range determined by positive finite endpoints; and trigonometric reduction examines a finite cell list determined by finite endpoints and a positive certified pi lower bound, returning a named failure if that bound or a branch is unresolved. Square-root endpoint bisection starts with finite integer indices and strictly decreases their positive gap until it is at most one ([[alg-dyadic-square-root-bisection]]). Thus these child calls terminate. The phase routine examines only the integer precisions from $p_{\phi,0}$ to $p_{\phi,\max}$ and calls those finite evaluators ([[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]]). Each FFT recursion either returns at length one, returns when its depth cap is zero, or makes two calls with the cap reduced by one and a finite twiddle loop. Induction on the finite depth cap therefore proves termination of every forward call; inverse mode adds only finite conjugations. A failed child call propagates its named status. Consequently no child in [F2]–[F3] is an unbounded evaluation oracle. [given, F2, F3, F4, induction, algebra]

1.2 Every loop in a candidate is finite: the dimension, source and mode lists, grid-cell lists, image ranges $[-L_r,L_r]$, expression DAGs, range truncation index $J$, phase precision interval $[p_{\phi,0},p_{\phi,\max}]$, and recursion cap $d_{\rm FFT}$ are finite by [F1]–[F3], while every FFT length is a finite power of two by [F3]. The finite norm sums used in the radius construction are defined by [F5]. Thus a candidate either returns a result or reaches one of its explicitly named failure branches after finitely many operations. [given, F1, F2, F3, F5, algebra]

1.3 Every division in step 1 is preceded by the denominator, $s_r<1$, and $d_{\min}^->0$ checks; every type-1 or type-2 mode division is preceded by its own positive-lower-endpoint test in steps 3–4. Hence all performed divisions have divisor intervals excluding zero. The FFT is called only on inputs in its model's representable set; its statuses are checked and no FFT output is used unless every returned twiddle certificate is at most $\epsilon_{\rm tw}$. The type-1 FFT-error radius uses the same checked call bounds [F6]; its normalization divisor is checked to have a strictly positive enclosure before division, and its finite upward radius sum is checked for overflow. A failed interval, range, FFT, denominator, mode-positivity, radius or twiddle check rejects the candidate. Sound containment of every returned finite interval follows from [F2] and [F4]. [given, F2, F3, F4, F6, algebra]

2.1 The ordered candidate list is finite, and processing terminates for each candidate by step 1.2. The procedure returns the first successful candidate whose outward absolute-error bound meets $\varepsilon_{\rm req}$; if none does so, it returns inconclusive with the first recorded non-success reason, including `requested-tolerance-not-met` when all computed bounds exceed tolerance. Therefore every certified return has passed its finite checks, and the inconclusive branch returns no approximation certified to the requested tolerance. [given, F1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional Gaussian probability
measure. Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be fixed, $k\ge2$, $p\ge2$,
$\ell=k+p\le\min(m,n)$, and draw $\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell}$ with
iid standard real Gaussian entries. If $Q$ is an orthonormal basis for
$\operatorname{Ran}(A\Omega)$, then
$$\mathbb E\|A-QQ^*A\|_2\le \left(1+\sqrt{\frac{k}{p-1}}\right)\sigma_{k+1} +\frac{e\sqrt{k+p}}{p}\left(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
The rank of $Q$ may be smaller than $\ell$; exact arithmetic is assumed.
The comparator $\sigma_{k+1}$ is the minimum spectral error among all
rank-at-most-$k$ approximations.

1.1 By [F9], $\sigma_{k+1}$ is the optimal rank-$k$ comparator. Choose an SVD $A=U\Sigma V^*$ and write $V^*\Omega=[\Omega_1^T\ \Omega_2^T]^T$ with $k$ top rows. By [F1] the blocks are independent standard Gaussian matrices; by [F2] and the wide-row-rank result $\Omega_1$ has full row rank almost surely. Thus [F6] gives $\|A-QQ^*A\|_2\le\sigma_{k+1}+\|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2$ off a null set. The error is bounded by $\|A\|_2$ for every draw, so the exceptional null set does not change its expectation. [given, F1, F2, F6, F9, A1, choose]

2.1 Fix $\Omega_1$ and integrate first over the independent block $\Omega_2$. By [F5], $\mathbb E_{\Omega_2}\|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2\le\|\Sigma_2\|_2\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F+\|\Sigma_2\|_F\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2$. Tonelli [F8] and the finite moments [F3]–[F4] justify this iterated expectation. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, F5, F8]

3.1 Take expectation over $\Omega_1$. By [F7] and [F3], $\mathbb E\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F\le\sqrt{k/(p-1)}$; [F4] supplies $\mathbb E\|\Omega_1^\dagger\|_2\le e\sqrt{k+p}/p$. Since $\|\Sigma_2\|_2=\sigma_{k+1}$ and $\|\Sigma_2\|_F=(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2)^{1/2}$, substituting into steps 1.1–2.1 gives the claimed bound. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F3, F4, F7, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedron and
let $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ be a shape-regular family of matching affine
tetrahedral meshes with maximum cell diameter $h\to0$, as in
[[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]] and the mesh hypothesis of
[[lem-pe11-smooth-nedelec-approximation]]. For each mesh
let $K_h=\ker(\operatorname{curl}|_{V_h})$ and
$X_h=V_h\cap K_h^\perp$, with the $L^2$ inner product. Then for every
$u\in X$ and every sequence of mesh sizes $h_n\to0$, there are
$u_{h_n}\in X_{h_n}$ such that
$$\|u_{h_n}-u\|_{H(\operatorname{curl};\Omega)}\longrightarrow0.$$

1.1 By [F1], for every $j\ge1$ there is $\varphi_j\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\|u-\varphi_j\|_{H(\operatorname{curl})}<1/j$. Countable Choice selects one such field for each $j$. By [F2], for each fixed $j$ there is an index $N_j$ such that for every $n\ge N_j$, $I_{h_n}\varphi_j\in V_{h_n}$ and $\|I_{h_n}\varphi_j-\varphi_j\|_{H(\operatorname{curl})}<1/j$; choose the least such $N_j$, and replace the sequence by increasing thresholds $M_j:=\max\{j,N_1,\ldots,N_j,M_{j-1}+1\}$, with $M_0=0$. [A1, F1, F2, given, choose]

1.2 Each $K_{h_n}$ is a finite-dimensional subspace of the real $L^2$ Hilbert space. By Countable Choice [A1], choose an orthonormal basis for each $K_{h_n}$ using [F3]. If a sequence in $K_{h_n}$ converges in $L^2$, its coordinates against this finite basis converge, and the limit is the corresponding finite linear combination; thus $K_{h_n}$ is closed. By [F3] it has an orthogonal projection $P_n$ satisfying $\|P_n y\|_2\le\|y\|_2$, including $P_n=0$ when $K_{h_n}=\{0\}$. [A1, F3, given, construct]

## Statement

For every assembled residual $f\in\widehat W'$, the unique minimizer over $w\in\widetilde W$ of

$$J_f(w)=\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S w,w\rangle-\langle f,E_0w\rangle$$

is $w_* = \widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$. The conforming correction returned by BDDC is $E_0 w_*=E_0\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$.

1.1 Differentiating the finite-dimensional quadratic in a direction $z\in\widetilde W$ gives $J_f'(w)[z]=\langle\widetilde S w,z\rangle-\langle f,E_0z\rangle$. Thus its critical point solves $\widetilde S w=E_0^Tf$, whose unique solution is $w_*=\widetilde S^{-1}E_0^T f$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 For any $z\in\widetilde W$, expansion about the critical point yields $J_f(w_*+z)=J_f(w_*)+\tfrac12\langle\widetilde S z,z\rangle$. By [F2] the added term is positive unless $z=0$, so $w_*$ is the unique global minimizer. Applying $E_0$ gives the displayed BDDC correction by [F1]. [given, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $D=(0,2)\times(0,1)$ be the union of two adjacent identity NURBS rectangles $D_L=(0,1)\times(0,1)$ and $D_R=(1,2)\times(0,1)$. Define $v=0$ on $D_L$ and $v=1$ on $D_R$. Then $v\in L^2(D)$ but $v\notin H^1(D)$, although the patch geometries match exactly. Thus matching physical geometry does not replace the matching-field-trace condition in [[def-isogeometric-galerkin-patch-space-and-refinement]].

1.1 The two constants are square integrable on their bounded rectangles, hence $v\in L^2(D)$. Choose $\eta\in C_c^\infty((0,1))$ with $\int_0^1\eta(y)\,dy\ne0$, and choose $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ with $\psi(0)=1$. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, set $\phi_\varepsilon(x,y)=\psi((x-1)/\varepsilon)\eta(y)\in C_c^\infty(D)$. [given, F2, construct]

2.1 Since $v$ vanishes for $x<1$ and equals one for $x>1$, a change of variable $t=(x-1)/\varepsilon$ gives $\int_Dv\,\partial_x\phi_\varepsilon\,dxdy=\left(\int_0^1\eta\right)\int_1^2\varepsilon^{-1}\psi'((x-1)/\varepsilon)dx=-\psi(0)\int_0^1\eta,$ which is a fixed nonzero number. If an $L^2$ weak derivative $g=\partial_xv$ existed, [F2] and Cauchy--Schwarz would make the absolute value at most $\|g\|_2\|\phi_\varepsilon\|_2$. But $\|\phi_\varepsilon\|_2=\sqrt\varepsilon\|\psi\|_2\|\eta\|_2\to0$, contradiction. Therefore $v\notin H^1(D)$. Its two constant traces across $x=1$ are 0 and 1, violating [F1] even though the geometry is matching; the sufficient condition of [F3] does not apply. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For $d=1$, one control, $\alpha=1$, and $b=0$ on $\mathbb T^1$, set
$$u(x,t)=e^{-t}\cos(2\pi x),\qquad f(x,t)=(-1+4\pi^2)e^{-t}\cos(2\pi x).$$
Then $u_t-(u_{xx}+f)=0$ exactly. On a periodic grid $h=1/N$, the centered
diffusion scheme with $0<\tau\le h^2/2$ satisfies a normalized one-step
residual of order $O(\tau+h^2)$ on the sampled exact solution. This is a
local residual calculation, not a global solution-error estimate.

1.1 Direct differentiation gives $u_t=-u$ and $u_{xx}=-4\pi^2u$. Therefore $u_t-u_{xx}=(-1+4\pi^2)u=f$, proving the exact PDE identity in [F1]. The diffusion-dominance condition is automatic since $b=0$; the CFL condition is $2\tau/h^2\le1$, which is exactly the stated time-step bound. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 The discrete second difference is $$D_{xx}^h u(x_i,t_n)= -\frac{4\sin^2(\pi h)}{h^2}u(x_i,t_n).$$ Taylor expansion in time gives $(u(x_i,t_n+\tau)-u(x_i,t_n))/\tau=u_t(x_i,t_n)+O(\tau)$, while $$u_{xx}-D_{xx}^h u= \left(\frac{4\sin^2(\pi h)}{h^2}-4\pi^2\right)u=O(h^2),$$ because $\sin z=z+O(z^3)$ at $z=0$. Thus the exact normalized residual is $O(\tau+h^2)$, agreeing with [F2]. No accumulated error is claimed. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $V,U_1,U_2$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces, let $A:V\to V'$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $L_i:V\to U_i$, $T_i:U_i\to V$ satisfy $L_iT_i=I_{U_i}$ for $i=1,2$ and $T_1L_1+T_2L_2=I_V$. Then the operators

$$G_1=(L_1A^{-1}L_1^T)(T_1^TAT_1),\qquad G_2=(T_2^TAT_2)(L_2A^{-1}L_2^T)$$

have the same eigenvalues, with the same multiplicities, except possibly at the eigenvalue $1$.

1.1 Set $X=L_1A^{-1}L_2^T:U_2\to U_1$ and $Y=T_2^TAT_1:U_1\to U_2$. By [F1] and [F2], $L_1T_1=I$, $L_2T_2=I$, and $T_1L_1+T_2L_2=I$. Expanding the products gives $G_1-I=-XY$ and $G_2-I=-YX$. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the nonsymmetric Nitsche setup of [[def-nitsche-boundary-penalty-forms]] and [[thm-nitsche-consistency-and-energy-quasioptimality]] with penalty above its coercivity threshold. Put $e:=u-u_h^0\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $\zeta_e\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ solve $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\nabla\zeta_e=\int_\Omega ve$ for all $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$. Let $s\in(1/2,1]$ and assume the genuine dual regularity hypothesis [A1]. The proved comparison interpolation theorem supplies $z_h:=I_{h,0}\zeta_e\in Y_h$ with $\|\zeta_e-z_h\|_{\#,h}\le C_D h^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}$, and the proved weighted flux trace theorem supplies
$$\left(\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^\partial}h_F\|\partial_n\zeta_e\|_{L^2(F)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_T h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)},\qquad 0<h\le\ell_\Omega:=\operatorname{diam}(\Omega).$$
Then
$$\|e\|_2\le\left(M_0C_DC_Rh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}+C_TC_Rh^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\right)\|e\|_{\#,h},$$
where $M_0:=2+\gamma_0\ge1$ and $C_D,C_T$ are mesh-uniform for the fixed domain. Since $s>1/2$ and $h\le\ell_\Omega$, the right side is $O(h^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2})\|e\|_{\#,h}$ after absorbing the fixed constants. The surviving boundary term prevents claiming the symmetric $h^s$ factor from dual regularity alone.

1.1 The adjoint equation is bounded and coercive on the Hilbert space $H^1_0(\Omega)$: Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the gradient form, and [F2] plus Poincaré makes it coercive in the usual $H^1$ norm. Its load $v\mapsto\int_\Omega ve$ is bounded by $\|v\|_{H^1}\|e\|_2$, so [F2] gives a unique weak solution; its stated higher regularity remains an assumption. Testing the equation with $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)\subset H^1_0(\Omega)$ gives $\int\nabla\phi\cdot\nabla\zeta_e=\int\phi e$, hence $-\Delta\zeta_e=e$ distributionally and [F6] applies. By [F3] the gradient has an $H^s(K)$ restriction on each cell, and [F4] gives its individual facet traces, which [F6] identifies as weak conormal traces. [F2, F3, F4, F6, given]

1.2 Green's identity [F6] for $\zeta_e$ with test $e$ gives $\|e\|_2^2=\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla\zeta_e-\sum_F\int_F e\,\partial_n\zeta_e$. For $z_h\in Y_h$, [F5] gives zero boundary trace, so $a_h^0(e,z_h)=\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla z_h$; the nonsymmetric flux term and penalty term vanish. Orthogonality [F1] therefore gives $\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla z_h=0$, and $\|e\|_2^2=\int_\Omega
abla e\cdot
abla(\zeta_e-z_h)-\sum_F\int_F e\,\partial_n\zeta_e.$ [F1, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 Cauchy–Schwarz and [F7] bound the volume term by $C_Dh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}\|e\|_{\#,h}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}$. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and [F8] bound the boundary term by $\left(\sum_Fh_F^{-1}\|e\|_F^2\right)^{1/2}\left(\sum_Fh_F\|\partial_n\zeta_e\|_F^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_Th^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2}\|e\|_{\#,h}\|\zeta_e\|_{H^{1+s}}.$ Use [A1] and $M_0\ge1$ to obtain $\|e\|_2^2\le(M_0C_DC_Rh^s\ell_\Omega^{1-s}+C_TC_Rh^{1/2}\ell_\Omega^{1/2})\|e\|_{\#,h}\|e\|_2$. If $\|e\|_2=0$ the conclusion is immediate; otherwise divide by it. Since $(h/\ell_\Omega)^s\le(h/\ell_\Omega)^{1/2}$ for $s>1/2$, the displayed half-order consequence follows. [A1, F7, F8, given, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $H_h(X,p)=\frac12p^TM^{-1}p+U_h(X)$ be [[def-periodic-pic-separable-hamiltonian-grid-model]], with $M$ symmetric positive definite and $U_h\in C^3(\mathbb R^{dP})$ periodic. Let $\Phi_{\Delta t}=K_{\Delta t/2}\circ D_{\Delta t}\circ K_{\Delta t/2}$ be the leapfrog map with the kick and drift conventions of [[def-leapfrog-step-map]]. Then:

1. For every signed step $\Delta t$, $\Phi_{\Delta t}^{-1}=\Phi_{-\Delta t}$.
2. Every step is symplectic.
3. Assuming Countable Choice, every step preserves Lebesgue volume on phase space.
4. On a finite interval $[0,T]$, if the exact and numerical paths, all kick/drift stages, and all line segments in the comparison lie in a common compact convex tube and the Hamiltonian vector field has bounded derivatives through order two there, the leapfrog trajectory error is at most $C_VTe^{LT}\Delta t^2$ for exact initialization and sufficiently small $\Delta t=T/n$.

The exact continuous flow conserves $H_h$ by [[thm-periodic-pic-hamiltonian-force-is-a-gradient-and-conserves-energy]]. No claim says the leapfrog map preserves $H_h$ exactly or that modified-energy estimates hold outside the analytic tube hypotheses of the geometric-integration suppliers.

1.1 The kicks and drifts in [F1] have inverses $K_{-a}$ and $D_{-b}$. Reversing the composition gives $\Phi_{\Delta t}^{-1}=K_{-\Delta t/2}\circ D_{-\Delta t}\circ K_{-\Delta t/2}=\Phi_{-\Delta t}$. All maps are global on the periodic lift, so no intermediate-domain restriction is lost. [F1, algebra]

1.2 The potential is smooth, hence $C^2$, and $M$ is symmetric positive definite. Each admitted kick and drift satisfies the symplectic Jacobian identity [F2]; composing the three maps preserves that identity by the chain rule, as stated in [F3]. [F1, F2, F3, given]

1.3 The Jacobian of a kick is $\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\-\frac{\Delta t}{2}\nabla^2U_h&I\end{pmatrix}$ and the Jacobian of a drift is $\begin{pmatrix}I&\Delta t M^{-1}\\0&I\end{pmatrix}$. Each is block triangular with identity diagonal blocks, so its determinant is $1$; multiplicativity gives $\det D\Phi_{\Delta t}=1$. The global kick/drift maps are $C^1$ diffeomorphisms, so [A1] permits applying [F5] to the map and its inverse, proving preservation of Lebesgue volume. [A1, F1, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 Under the tube and smoothness hypotheses, [F4] gives the stated global order-two error bound. The continuous invariant is the separate identity [F6]; it is not an assertion about the discrete map. [F4, F6, given] ∎

## Statement

The improper integral is
$$\int_0^1x^{-1/2}\log x\,dx=-4.$$
For example, [[alg-endpoint-power-regularized-jacobi-quadrature]] applies with $n=1$, $\alpha=-1/2$, $\beta=0$, $m_a=1$, $m_b=0$, $h(x)=1$, $q_a=7$, and $q_b=4$. The transformed functions are $C^2$ and [[thm-endpoint-regularized-jacobi-error]] gives an explicit error bound $C_1(\|F_L''\|_\infty+\|F_R''\|_\infty)$ for the returned two-node sum.

1.1 A primitive on $(0,1]$ is $P(x)=2\sqrt{x}\log x-4\sqrt{x}$ by [F1] and [F6]. The endpoint term $\sqrt{x}\log x$ tends to zero by the power-regularity lemma [F2] with $r=0$, $\delta=1/2$, and polynomial $z$. Hence $P(x)\to0$ as $x\downarrow0$. Applying [F5] on $[\varepsilon,1]$ and taking $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives the improper integral $P(1)-0=-4$. [F1, F2, F5, F6, algebra]

1.2 For the left substitution, $\delta_L=q_a(\alpha+1)-1=7/2-1=5/2>2$; its transformed function is a constant times $t^{5/2}$ times a polynomial of degree one in $\log t$ and a smooth factor bounded with two continuous derivatives. For the right substitution, $\delta_R=q_b(\beta+1)-1=3>2$ and the remaining factors are smooth on $[0,1]$. Therefore both transformed functions are $C^2$ by [F2], and [F3] applies. [F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F4] with $n=1$ to the functions in step 1.2. Its error constant is $C_1$ and the output is the stated sum, so the claimed error bound follows. The value $-4$ from step 1.1 is the integral being approximated. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, bounded, connected and Lipschitz, $d=2$ or $3$, and let $\nu>0$. For every bounded linear functional $F$ on $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ equipped with $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_2$, there is a unique $(u,p)\in V\times Q$, $Q=L^2_0(D)$, satisfying
$$2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(u):\varepsilon(v)-\int_Dp\operatorname{div}v=F(v),\qquad -\int_Dq\operatorname{div}u=0$$
for every $v\in V,q\in Q$. The pressure is normalized to have mean zero. One stability bound is $\|u\|_V\le\nu^{-1}\|F\|_{V'}$ and $\|p\|_2\le3C_{\rm div}(D)\|F\|_{V'}$.

1.1 By [F1], $V$ is complete in the H1 norm. If $(v_n)$ is Cauchy in $\|\nabla\cdot\|_2$, [F1] and Poincare make it Cauchy in H1; its H1 limit is in the closed subspace $H^1_0$ and its gradients converge. Thus $V$ is Hilbert in the gradient norm. By [F2], $Q$ is Hilbert. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Cauchy–Schwarz and $|\varepsilon(v)|\le|

u(u,v)|\le2
u\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$. By [F3], $a_

u\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2^2\ge
u\|v\|_V^2$ on all of $V$, hence on $\ker B$; take $M_a=2

3.1 The form $b$ has $M_b\le\sqrt d$ and inf-sup $\beta\ge C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1}$ by [F4]. Apply [F5] with $G=0$. It yields a unique velocity and a unique mean-zero pressure satisfying the two displayed equations. The bound on velocity is $\|u\|_V\le\alpha^{-1}\|F\|=\nu^{-1}\|F\|$. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 By [F6], $\operatorname{div}u\in Q$. The constraint equation tested with $q=\operatorname{div}u$ therefore gives $\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2^2=0$, so the weak constraint is exact incompressibility. Also [F5] gives $\|p\|_2\le\beta^{-1}(\|F\|+M_a\|u\|_V)$. Use $\beta^{-1}\le C_{\rm div}(D)$, $M_a=2\nu$ and the velocity estimate of step 3.1 to obtain $\|p\|_2\le3C_{\rm div}(D)\|F\|$. Mean-zero gauge is part of $Q$, so the pressure is unique in that normalization. [A1, F4, F5, F6, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice.

On $K=\{(x,y):x>0,y>0,x+y<1\}$ with unit permeability, $q=(1,0)$ and $p=-x$ satisfy $q+\nabla p=0$ and $\operatorname{div}q=0$. Their outward integrated facet fluxes on $x=0$, $y=0$, and $x+y=1$ are respectively $-1,0,+1$, so exact local mass balance holds.

1.1 The gradient is $\nabla p=(-1,0)$, so $q+\nabla p=0$ pointwise. The three outward unit normals are $(-1,0)$ on $x=0$, $(0,-1)$ on $y=0$, and $(1,1)/\sqrt2$ on the hypotenuse. Their facet lengths are $1,1,\sqrt2$, respectively. Therefore the integrated fluxes are $-1$, $0$, and $(1/\sqrt2)\sqrt2=1$. [given, algebra]

2.1 Their sum is zero, equal to $\int_K\operatorname{div}q=0$ by [F2]. Since $q$ is in RT0 and the fluxes are its facet degrees of freedom by [F1], the data also uniquely determine this constant flux among RT0 fields. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V_h,Q_h$ be the stable mini-element spaces on a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain with a conforming mesh, with viscosity $\nu>0$, and let $Z_h=\{v_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\ \forall q_h\in Q_h\}$. Choose bases of $V_h,Q_h$, let $M$ be the velocity mass matrix, $A$ the Stokes stiffness matrix, and $B$ the constraint matrix with entries $B_{\ell j}=b(\phi_j,\chi_\ell)$. The mass-orthogonal projector onto $Z_h$ is
$$P_M=I-M^{-1}B^T(BM^{-1}B^T)^{-1}B.$$
On the mean-zero pressure coordinates, both the mass pressure Schur matrix $BM^{-1}B^T$ and stiffness pressure Schur matrix $BA^{-1}B^T$ are positive definite. Before imposing the pressure gauge on the full continuous P1 space, the constant pressure is exactly the one-dimensional nullspace of $B^T$.

1.1 The mass matrix $M$ is symmetric positive definite because for a nonzero coefficient vector $x$, $x^TMx=\|v_h(x)\|_{L^2}^2>0$. The inf-sup condition in [F1] says that $B^Ty=0$ for a mean-zero pressure coefficient vector $y$ implies $y=0$; hence $B$ has full row rank on the gauged pressure coordinates. [A1, F1, given]

2.1 Therefore $S_M:=BM^{-1}B^T$ is symmetric positive definite: for $y\ne0$, $y^TS_My=(B^Ty)^TM^{-1}(B^Ty)>0$. The formula for $P_M$ is defined. Direct multiplication gives $BP_M=B-BM^{-1}B^TS_M^{-1}B=0$, and if $Bx=0$ then $P_Mx=x$. Thus its range is exactly $\ker B$. [algebra, step 1.1]

3.1 For every $x$, $x-P_Mx=M^{-1}B^TS_M^{-1}Bx$. If $z\in\ker B$, then $z^TM(x-P_Mx)=(Bz)^TS_M^{-1}Bx=0$. Hence $x-P_Mx$ is mass-orthogonal to the kernel and $P_M$ is the mass-orthogonal projector. [algebra, step 2.1]

3.2 By [F3], $A$ is symmetric positive definite. Full row rank of $B$ from step 2.1 then makes $S_A:=BA^{-1}B^T$ positive definite by the same quadratic-form argument as in step 2.1. Eliminating velocity from $Au+B^Tp=f$, $Bu=g$ gives $S_Ap=BA^{-1}f-g$, which is the pressure Schur identity. [A1, F3, algebra, step 2.1]

4.1 If pressure coordinates are instead taken in the full continuous P1 space, [F2] puts constants in $\ker B^T$. Conversely, if $B^Ty=0$, the corresponding $q_h\in S^1_h$ pairs to zero with every velocity. Its mean-zero part $q_h-|D|^{-1}\int_Dq_h$ also pairs to zero by [F2]; the stable inf-sup in [F1] forces that part to vanish. Thus the nullspace consists exactly of constants, and restricting to $Q_h=L^2_0\cap S^1_h$ removes that gauge mode. [A1, F1, F2, algebra, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the model and mixed conventions of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]] and [[def-linear-elasticity-near-incompressible-mixed-mini-pair]]. Let $D$ be bounded, connected, and Lipschitz, $d\in\{2,3\}$, $0<\mu_0\le\mu\le\mu_1$, and $f\in V'$. For every $\lambda\in[0,\infty]$ the continuous problem has a unique solution; at $\lambda=0$ use the primal problem and set $p_0=0$, while at $\lambda=\infty$ impose $\operatorname{div}u=0$. If $D$ is polygonal or polyhedral and $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ is any conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family with a common shape-regularity bound, the mini-element discrete problem has a unique solution for every $h$ and every $\lambda\in[0,\infty]$, with $p_{h,0}=0$. There is a constant $C$ depending only on $d,D,\mu_0,\mu_1$ and the common shape-regularity bound, but independent of $\lambda$ and $h$, such that
$$\|u_\lambda\|_V+\|p_\lambda\|_Q\le C\|f\|_{V'},\qquad \|u_\lambda-u_{h,\lambda}\|_V+\|p_\lambda-p_{h,\lambda}\|_Q\le C\inf_{v_h\in V_h,\,q_h\in Q_h}\bigl(\|u_\lambda-v_h\|_V+\|p_\lambda-q_h\|_Q\bigr).$$
At $\lambda=\infty$ the constraint is $\operatorname{div}u=0$. The estimate makes no heterogeneous-coefficient robustness claim beyond the displayed dependence.

1.1 The pointwise bounds $|\varepsilon(v)|_F\le|\nabla v|_F$ and $|\operatorname{div}v|\le\sqrt d|\nabla v|_F$, together with [F9], give $|a_\mu(u,v)|\le2\mu_1\|u\|_V\|v\|_V$ and $|b(v,q)|\le\sqrt d\|v\|_V\|q\|_Q$. By [F3], $a_\mu(v,v)\ge2\mu_0\|\varepsilon(v)\|_2^2\ge\mu_0\|v\|_V^2$. [given, F1, F3, F9, algebra]

1.2 The space $V$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and its gradient norm is equivalent to the $H^1$ norm by [F8]; $Q$ is the closed kernel of the bounded integral functional on $L^2(D)$. Thus both are real Hilbert spaces under [A1]. Also $Q\ne\{0\}$: two disjoint positive-measure balls inside $D$ give a nonzero difference of indicator functions with zero integral. And $V\ne\{0\}$: choose a ball $B(x_0,r)$ with closure in $D$ and set $\phi(x)=\exp(-1/(r^2-|x-x_0|^2))$ inside it and zero outside. Its derivatives vanish at the sphere, so $\phi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ is nonzero and $(\phi,0,\ldots,0)\in V$. [A1, F8, F9, given, construct]

1.3 For finite $\lambda>0$, take the primal solution from [F7] and set $p_\lambda=-\lambda\operatorname{div}u_\lambda$. By [F2, F10], $p_\lambda\in Q$. Then $a_\mu(u_\lambda,v)+b(v,p_\lambda)=a_\mu(u_\lambda,v)+\lambda(\operatorname{div}u_\lambda,\operatorname{div}v)=f(v)$, while $b(u_\lambda,q)-\lambda^{-1}(p_\lambda,q)=-(\operatorname{div}u_\lambda,q)+(\operatorname{div}u_\lambda,q)=0$. Conversely, any mixed solution has $s=\operatorname{div}u+\lambda^{-1}p\in Q$ by [F2]; its second equation gives $(s,q)=0$ for every $q\in Q$, hence $s=0$ by choosing $q=s$. It therefore solves the unique primal equation and has the same pressure. [A1, F2, F7, F10, given, algebra]

2.1 At $\lambda=0$, use the primal solution and set $p_0=0$ by convention. At $\lambda=\infty$, apply [F6] to $V,Q$, $a=a_\mu$, and $b$ with $G=0$: [F1] and step 1.1 give bounded forms, step 1.1 gives coercivity on all of $V$, [F4] gives the inf-sup bound, and step 1.2 gives real Hilbert spaces with both $V,Q$ nonzero. This yields a unique mean-zero pair $(u_\infty,p_\infty)$. [A1, F1, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 For each discrete pair, [F5] supplies a positive $\beta_h$ bounded below independently of $h$. For finite $\lambda>0$ or $\lambda=\infty$, write $c=\lambda^{-1}\ge0$, with $c=0$ at infinity. A homogeneous discrete mixed solution $(w_h,r_h)$ satisfies $a_\mu(w_h,v_h)+b(v_h,r_h)=0$ and $b(w_h,q_h)-c(r_h,q_h)=0$. Test with $v_h=w_h$ and $q_h=r_h$ and subtract the second equality from the first to get $a_\mu(w_h,w_h)+c\|r_h\|_Q^2=0$. Step 1.1 forces $w_h=0$, and then discrete inf-sup forces $r_h=0$. The square finite-dimensional block matrix is injective, hence bijective, so the discrete system has a unique solution for every right-hand side. [A1, F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.3 The same stability estimate applies to any solution of $a_\mu(w,v)+b(v,r)=F(v)$, $b(w,q)-c(r,q)=G(q)$ when the inf-sup constant is $\beta>0$. Put $U=\|w\|_V$, $P=\|r\|_Q$, $F_0=\|F\|_{V'}$, and $G_0=\|G\|_{Q'}$. Testing with $v=w$ and $q=r$ and subtracting gives $\mu_0U^2\le F_0U+G_0P$. The first equation and inf-sup give $\beta P\le F_0+2\mu_1U$. With $S=F_0+G_0$ and $A=1+2\mu_1/\beta$, substitution, using $F_0G_0\le S^2/4$, yields $\mu_0U^2\le ASU+S^2/(4\beta)$. Solving this quadratic gives $U\le C_US$, where $C_U=(A+\sqrt{A^2+\mu_0/\beta})/(2\mu_0)$; then $P\le C_PS$ with $C_P=\beta^{-1}(1+2\mu_1C_U)$. Thus $U+P\le C_*S$ for $C_*=C_U+C_P$, and these constants do not depend on $c$. [F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For $0<\lambda\le\mu_0$, let $P_h:Q\to Q_h$ be the $L^2$-orthogonal projection. It exists uniquely: in a basis of the finite-dimensional $Q_h$, its defining normal equations have the positive-definite Gram matrix $((q_i,q_j))$, and orthogonality gives $\|p-P_hp\|_Q=\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q$. The second mixed equation gives $p_h=-\lambda P_h\operatorname{div}u_h$. Hence the first is the symmetric discrete equation $a_h(u_h,v_h)=f(v_h)$, where $a_h(w,v)=a_\mu(w,v)+\lambda(P_h\operatorname{div}w,P_h\operatorname{div}v)$. It is bounded by $M_0=2\mu_1+d\mu_0$ and coercive by $\mu_0$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F9, step 1.3, step 2.2, construct]

4.1 For any $w_h\in V_h$, subtract the equation for $a_h(w_h,\cdot)$ from the continuous primal equation. For every $v_h\in V_h$ this gives $a_h(u_h-w_h,v_h)=a_h(u-w_h,v_h)+\lambda((I-P_h)\operatorname{div}u,(I-P_h)\operatorname{div}v_h)$. Since $p=-\lambda\operatorname{div}u$, $\lambda(I-P_h)\operatorname{div}u=-(I-P_h)p$; orthogonal projection gives $\|I-P_h\|\le1$, while $\|\operatorname{div}v_h\|_2\le\sqrt d\|v_h\|_V$, so Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the remainder by $\sqrt d\|p-P_hp\|_Q\|v_h\|_V$. Testing with $v_h=u_h-w_h$ and using coercivity yields the displacement estimate; if $u_h=w_h$ it is immediate, and otherwise divide by $\mu_0\|u_h-w_h\|_V$ and take the infimum over $w_h$: $\|u-u_h\|_V\le\left(1+\frac{M_0}{\mu_0}\right)\inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|u-w_h\|_V+\frac{\sqrt d}{\mu_0}\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q$. Moreover, $p-p_h=(I-P_h)p-\lambda P_h\operatorname{div}(u-u_h)$, so $\|p-p_h\|_Q\le\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q+\mu_0\sqrt d\|u-u_h\|_V$. Adding these bounds gives the claimed product-space best-approximation estimate with a constant depending only on $d,\mu_0,\mu_1$. [A1, F1, F2, F9, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Testing the continuous primal equation with $u$ and the equivalent discrete $a_h$ equation with $u_h$, coercivity gives $\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V\le\mu_0^{-1}\|f\|_{V'}$. The pressure identities and $\lambda\le\mu_0$ then give $\|p\|_Q\le\lambda\sqrt d\|u\|_V\le\sqrt d\|f\|_{V'}$ and $\|p_h\|_Q\le\lambda\sqrt d\|u_h\|_V\le\sqrt d\|f\|_{V'}$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F9, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For $\lambda=0$, [F7] gives the solution bounds and the displacement estimate with constant $2\mu_1/\mu_0$; $p_0=p_{h,0}=0$. For $0<\lambda\le\mu_0$, step 4.2 gives uniform solution bounds and step 4.1 the uniform best-approximation estimate. For $\lambda\ge\mu_0$ or $\lambda=\infty$, step 2.3 with the continuous inf-sup bound [F4] and discrete bound [F5] gives uniform solution bounds. For the same upper range, $c=\lambda^{-1}\le\mu_0^{-1}$ and $|\mathcal A_\lambda((u,p),(v,q))|\le2\mu_1\|u\|_V\|v\|_V+\sqrt d\|v\|_V\|p\|_Q+\sqrt d\|u\|_V\|q\|_Q+\mu_0^{-1}\|p\|_Q\|q\|_Q$, so its product-space operator norm is at most $M=2\mu_1+2\sqrt d+\mu_0^{-1}$, independently of $\lambda$. [A1, F4, F5, F7, F9, step 2.3, step 4.1, step 4.2, algebra]

6.1 Write $\|(v,q)\|_{V\times Q}=\|v\|_V+\|q\|_Q$. Let $x=(u,p)$ be the continuous solution, $x_h=(u_h,p_h)$ its Galerkin solution, and fix $y_h=(v_h,q_h)\in V_h\times Q_h$. Galerkin orthogonality gives $\mathcal A_\lambda(x_h-y_h,z_h)=\mathcal A_\lambda(x-y_h,z_h)$ for every $z_h=(w_h,r_h)$. Thus $x_h-y_h$ solves the discrete mixed system with data $F_h(w_h)=\mathcal A_\lambda(x-y_h,(w_h,0))$ and $G_h(r_h)=\mathcal A_\lambda(x-y_h,(0,r_h))$. The bound on $\mathcal A_\lambda$ gives $\|F_h\|+\|G_h\|\le2M\|x-y_h\|_{V\times Q}$. Applying the stability bound of step 2.3 with $\beta\ge\min(C_{\rm div}(D)^{-1},\beta_*)>0$, then the triangle inequality and the infimum over $y_h$, gives the required estimate with a constant at most $1+2MC_*$. Combining this with steps 1.3–2.1, 2.2, 4.1–4.2, and 5.1 covers every $\lambda\in[0,\infty]$. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.3, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

It therefore solves the unique primal equation and has the same pressure. [A1, F2, F7, F10, given, algebra]

2.1 At $\lambda=0$, use the primal solution and set $p_0=0$ by convention. At $\lambda=\infty$, apply [F6] to $V,Q$, $a=a_\mu$, and $b$ with $G=0$: [F1] and step 1.1 give bounded forms, step 1.1 gives coercivity on all of $V$, [F4] gives the inf-sup bound, and step 1.2 gives real Hilbert spaces with both $V,Q$ nonzero. This yields a unique mean-zero pair $(u_\infty,p_\infty)$. [A1, F1, F4, F6, step 1.1, step 1.2]

2.2 For each discrete pair, [F5] supplies a positive $\beta_h$ bounded below independently of $h$. For finite $\lambda>0$ or $\lambda=\infty$, write $c=\lambda^{-1}\ge0$, with $c=0$ at infinity. A homogeneous discrete mixed solution $(w_h,r_h)$ satisfies $a_\mu(w_h,v_h)+b(v_h,r_h)=0$ and $b(w_h,q_h)-c(r_h,q_h)=0$. Test with $v_h=w_h$ and $q_h=r_h$ and subtract the second equality from the first to get $a_\mu(w_h,w_h)+c\|r_h\|_Q^2=0$. Step 1.1 forces $w_h=0$, and then discrete inf-sup forces $r_h=0$. The square finite-dimensional block matrix is injective, hence bijective, so the discrete system has a unique solution for every right-hand side. [A1, F5, step 1.1, given, algebra]

2.3 The same stability estimate applies to any solution of $a_\mu(w,v)+b(v,r)=F(v)$, $b(w,q)-c(r,q)=G(q)$ when the inf-sup constant is $\beta>0$. Put $U=\|w\|_V$, $P=\|r\|_Q$, $F_0=\|F\|_{V'}$, and $G_0=\|G\|_{Q'}$. Testing with $v=w$ and $q=r$ and subtracting gives $\mu_0U^2\le F_0U+G_0P$. The first equation and inf-sup give $\beta P\le F_0+2\mu_1U$. With $S=F_0+G_0$ and $A=1+2\mu_1/\beta$, substitution, using $F_0G_0\le S^2/4$, yields $\mu_0U^2\le ASU+S^2/(4\beta)$. Solving this quadratic gives $U\le C_US$, where $C_U=(A+\sqrt{A^2+\mu_0/\beta})/(2\mu_0)$; then $P\le C_PS$ with $C_P=\beta^{-1}(1+2\mu_1C_U)$. Thus $U+P\le C_*S$ for $C_*=C_U+C_P$, and these constants do not depend on $c$. [F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

It exists uniquely: in a basis of the finite-dimensional $Q_h$, its defining normal equations have the positive-definite Gram matrix $((q_i,q_j))$, and orthogonality gives $\|p-P_hp\|_Q=\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q$. The second mixed equation gives $p_h=-\lambda P_h\operatorname{div}u_h$. Hence the first is the symmetric discrete equation $a_h(u_h,v_h)=f(v_h)$, where $a_h(w,v)=a_\mu(w,v)+\lambda(P_h\operatorname{div}w,P_h\operatorname{div}v)$. For every $v_h\in V_h$ this gives $a_h(u_h-w_h,v_h)=a_h(u-w_h,v_h)+\lambda((I-P_h)\operatorname{div}u,(I-P_h)\operatorname{div}v_h)$. Since $p=-\lambda\operatorname{div}u$, $\lambda(I-P_h)\operatorname{div}u=-(I-P_h)p$; orthogonal projection gives $\|I-P_h\|\le1$, while $\|\operatorname{div}v_h\|_2\le\sqrt d\|v_h\|_V$, so Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the remainder by $\sqrt d\|p-P_hp\|_Q\|v_h\|_V$. Testing with $v_h=u_h-w_h$ and using coercivity yields the displacement estimate; if $u_h=w_h$ it is immediate, and otherwise divide by $\mu_0\|u_h-w_h\|_V$ and take the infimum over $w_h$: $\|u-u_h\|_V\le\left(1+\frac{M_0}{\mu_0}\right)\inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|u-w_h\|_V+\frac{\sqrt d}{\mu_0}\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q$. Moreover, $p-p_h=(I-P_h)p-\lambda P_h\operatorname{div}(u-u_h)$, so $\|p-p_h\|_Q\le\inf_{q_h\in Q_h}\|p-q_h\|_Q+\mu_0\sqrt d\|u-u_h\|_V$. Adding these bounds gives the claimed product-space best-approximation estimate with a constant depending only on $d,\mu_0,\mu_1$. [A1, F1, F2, F9, step 1.3, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Testing the continuous primal equation with $u$ and the equivalent discrete $a_h$ equation with $u_h$, coercivity gives $\|u\|_V,\|u_h\|_V\le\mu_0^{-1}\|f\|_{V'}$. The pressure identities and $\lambda\le\mu_0$ then give $\|p\|_Q\le\lambda\sqrt d\|u\|_V\le\sqrt d\|f\|_{V'}$ and $\|p_h\|_Q\le\lambda\sqrt d\|u_h\|_V\le\sqrt d\|f\|_{V'}$. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be a
bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal or polyhedral domain with a finite,
nonempty conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh. Use the MINI spaces
$(V_h,Q_h)$ of
[[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]], the Stokes norms and bilinear
forms of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], and the
viscous velocity form
$$ a_\nu(v,w)=2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(v):\varepsilon(w),\qquad \nu>0. $$
Let $A_h,B_h$ be the matrices of $a_\nu$ and
$b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ in any bases, and let $M_Q$ be the
$L^2(D)$ pressure mass matrix. Use the symmetric saddle convention of
[[def-na-symmetric-saddle-point-system-and-block-preconditioners]]. With
$S_h=B_hA_h^{-1}B_h^T$, the steady Stokes
pressure Schur complement satisfies
$$ \frac{(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-2}}{\nu(1+d)}M_Q \preceq S_h\preceq \frac d\nu M_Q. $$
Here $C_F$ is the shape-regularity-uniform Fortin norm bound and
$C_{\rm div}(D)$ is the continuous divergence right-inverse bound in
[[thm-na-mini-element-fortin-stability]]. The result is for the steady
velocity stiffness; it asserts no corresponding bound for an unsteady shifted
Schur complement.

1.1 The given finite nonempty mesh contains at least one $d$-simplex, so $N_K\ge1$ and $N_v\ge d+1$. The dimension formulas [F3] give $\dim V_h\ge d>0$ and $\dim Q_h\ge d>0$, verifying the dimension hypotheses in [F9]. For every nonzero pressure coefficient vector $q$, $q^TM_Qq=\|q_h\|_2^2>0$ by the pressure norm in [F1], so $M_Q$ is SPD. For every $v\in V_h$, [F4] and coordinate Cauchy--Schwarz [F7] give $|\operatorname{div}v|^2\le d|
abla v|^2$ pointwise. Integrating this inequality and using [F4] yields $$ 
u\|
abla v\|_2^2\le a_
u(v,v) \le 
u(1+d)\|
abla v\|_2^2. $$ The first inequality drops the nonnegative divergence term in [F4]; the second integrates the pointwise estimate. Thus $\alpha=
u$ and $\Lambda=
u(1+d)$ in [F6]. [A1, F1, F3, F4, F6, F7, F9, given, algebra]

1.2 For $v\in V_h$ and $q\in Q_h$, Holder's inequality [F8] and the same pointwise divergence bound give $$ |b(v,q)|\le\|q\|_2\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2 \le\sqrt d\|q\|_2\|\nabla v\|_2. $$ Hence the continuity constant in [F6] is $C_b=\sqrt d$. [F1, F2, F6, F8, algebra]

2.1 By [F5] and the definition [F10], the inf-sup constant in [F6] is at least $\beta=(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-1}>0$. If $B_h^Tq=0$ for a nonzero pressure vector, then $b(v,q)=q^TB_hv=0$ for every $v$, making the supremum in [F10] zero and contradicting this positive lower bound. Thus $B_h$ has full row rank as required by [F9]. The lower bound in step 1.1 makes $A_h$ positive definite. Apply [F6] with the constants established in steps 1.1–1.2. Its lower coefficient is $(C_FC_{\rm div}(D))^{-2}/(\nu(1+d))$ and its upper coefficient is $d/\nu$. This is the asserted steady pressure-mass Schur bound. [A1, F5, F6, F9, F10, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Example

Let $\widetilde W=\mathbb R^2$, $\widetilde S=A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$, $\widehat W=\operatorname{span}(e_1)$, $R=e_1$, $E_0=(1\;0)$, $B=(0\;1)$, and $B_D^T=e_2$. Then $E_0R=1$, $BB_D^T=1$, and $R E_0+B_D^TB=I$. The single BDDC and FETI-DP preconditioned eigenvalues both equal $4/3$.

1.1 The determinant of $A$ is $3$, so $A^{-1}=\tfrac13\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$. The BDDC coarse operator is $R^TAR=2$, while $E_0A^{-1}E_0^T=2/3$; their product is $4/3$. [given, F1, algebra]

1.2 The dual operator is $BA^{-1}B^T=2/3$, and its preconditioner is $B_DAB_D^T=2$; their product is also $4/3$. Direct multiplication gives the three identities in the Example, so the abstract assumptions hold. [given, F2, algebra]

2.1 Both operators are one-dimensional, hence each has the single eigenvalue computed in steps 1.1 and 1.2. The common value is positive and different from $1$, consistent with [F3]. [given, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Example

Take $f=0$ and any initial weak-kernel velocity $u_h^0\in Z_h$. Every backward Euler MINI solution satisfies
$$\frac12\|u_h^m\|_2^2+\frac12\sum_{n=1}^m\|u_h^n-u_h^{n-1}\|_2^2+\nu\sum_{n=1}^m\tau_n\|\nabla u_h^n\|_2^2\le\frac12\|u_h^0\|_2^2.$$

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be nonempty, bounded, connected, Lipschitz and polyhedral, and let $0<T<\infty$. Let $\{\mathcal T_j\}$ be matching shape-regular affine simplicial meshes with $h_j\to0$, and let the time partitions of $[0,T]$ have maximum step tending to zero, with no relation required between the two limits. Let $f\in L^2(0,T;L^2(D)^d)$ and $u_0\in H_\sigma$. On each mesh take $u_j^0=P_{Z_j}u_0$, the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto the weak MINI kernel, and choose any backward Euler MINI solution from [[thm-na-mini-be-step-existence-energy]]. Then a subsequence of piecewise-constant velocities converges strongly in $L^2(0,T;L^2(D)^d)$ and weakly in $L^2(0,T;H^1_0(D)^d)$ to a velocity $u$ satisfying the solenoidal weak momentum equation, initial trace and energy inequality in [[def-na-solenoidal-energy-weak-ns-velocity]]. This theorem supplies the velocity limit and its energy inequality. It does not assert the pressure regularity and pressure-bearing formulation required by the PE06 plan; the remaining pressure obligation is explicitly escalated on the A page.

1.1 Since $u_0\in H_\sigma=\overline{V_\sigma}^{L^2}$, for any $\epsilon>0$ choose $v\in V_\sigma$ with $\|u_0-v\|_2<\epsilon$. By [F3], $\Pi_jv\in Z_j$ and $\|\Pi_jv-v\|_2\to0$. The best-approximation property [F4] gives $\|P_{Z_j}u_0-u_0\|_2\le\|\Pi_jv-u_0\|_2\le\|\Pi_jv-v\|_2+\epsilon$. Letting $j\to\infty$ and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$ proves strong convergence of the discrete initial data. [A1, F3, F4, given, choose]

1.2 Apply [F1] to every mesh and partition. The energy inequality gives uniform bounds for $\max_n\|u_j^n\|_2$ and $\|\overline u_j\|_{L^2V}$; it also gives $\|\overline u_j\|_{L^\infty H}\le M$. [F1, given]

1.3 Fix a finite orthonormal family $e_1,\ldots,e_m\in V_\sigma$. For each mesh, $\Pi_je_i\in Z_j$ by [F3], so testing the discrete equation [F13] with $\Pi_je_i$ removes pressure. The backward difference of $a_{j,i}^n=(u_j^n,\Pi_je_i)_2$ is therefore bounded by $|(D_\tau a_{j,i}^n)|\le C_{e_i}\big(\|f_j^n\|_2+\nu\|u_j^n\|_V+\|u_j^n\|_2^{1/2}\|u_j^n\|_V^{3/2}\big).$ The first two terms are bounded in $L^2(0,T)$ by [F1], and the last in $L^{4/3}(0,T)$ by [F11], because its $4/3$ power is at most $M^{2/3}C\|u_j^n\|_V^2$. Thus the coefficient condition of [F2] holds for every finite family. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F11, F13, given, algebra]

1.4 By [F2], after a subsequence $\overline u_j\to u$ strongly in $L^2(0,T;L^2)$. The energy bounds [F1] and [F9] give, after a further subsequence, $\overline u_j\rightharpoonup u$ in $L^2(0,T;V)$. Apply [F10] to the scalar functions $t\mapsto\|\overline u_j(t)-u(t)\|_2$ to obtain almost-everywhere-in-time strong convergence along a further subsequence. The uniform $L^\infty H$ bound then implies $u\in L^\infty(0,T;H)$. [A1, F1, F2, F9, F10]

2.1 For any $q\in C_c^\infty(D)$, apply the face-average interpolant to $q-|D|^{-1}\int_Dq$ and subtract the mean of its interpolant to obtain $q_j\in Q_j$ converging in $L^2$, using the approximation estimate in [[lem-na-scott-zhang-boundary-preserving-p1-interpolant]]. Since $b(u_j^n,q_j)=0$, [F6] gives $\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}u_j^n=0$ for the $q_j$ part and $\int_D\operatorname{div}u_j^n=0$ for the mean part. The $L^2$ approximation error times the uniformly bounded $L^2(0,T;V)$ divergence norm tends to zero by Holder. Passing to the weak gradient limit proves $\operatorname{div}u=0$ a.e.; hence $u\in L^2(0,T;V_\sigma)$. [F1, F6, step 1.4, F5]

2.2 Let $v\in V_\sigma$ and $\eta\in C^1([0,T])$ vanish near $T$. Test each time step [F13] by $\Pi_jv\in Z_j$, multiply by the left-endpoint value $\eta(t_{n-1}^j)$, and sum. Discrete summation by parts gives $-(u_j^0,\Pi_jv)_2\eta(0)-\sum_{n=1}^{N_j-1}(u_j^n,\Pi_jv)_2(\eta(t_n^j)-\eta(t_{n-1}^j))$; the terminal term is zero for all fine partitions because $\eta$ vanishes near $T$. The sum is exactly the integral of $-\overline u_j\cdot\Pi_jv\,\eta'$ on the nonterminal cells, so the time contribution converges to $-(u_0,v)_2\eta(0)-\int_0^T(u,v)_2\eta'$. Moving its initial term to the right side gives the required positive initial trace. Uniform convergence of the left-endpoint step approximation to $\eta$, [F3], and step 1.1 justify these limits. The viscosity term converges by weak $L^2V$ convergence and $\Pi_jv\to v$ in $V$; the force averages converge by [F7] and the same uniform time-test approximation. [F1, F3, F7, F13, step 1.1, step 1.4, algebra]

2.3 For almost every $t$, choose the first time node $t_j(t)\ge t$ and sum the work-form energy inequality of [F1] through that node. Then $\overline u_j(t)=u_j^{n_j(t)}$, so step 1.4 gives the required strong convergence of the kinetic-energy term for almost every $t$. By [F7], $f_j\to f$ in $L^2H$ and $\overline u_j\to u$ in $L^2H$, so their work integrals converge on $[0,t]$. The overshoot interval $[t,t_j(t)]$ contributes at most $\|f_j\|_{L^2H}M\sqrt{\tau_{\max}^j}$ by Cauchy--Schwarz and the uniform $L^\infty H$ bound, hence tends to zero. The gradient sum through $t_j(t)$ is bounded below by its integral through $t$; weak $L^2V$ convergence and [F9] give lower semicontinuity on $[0,t]$. The initial projections converge by step 1.1. This proves the energy inequality for almost every $t$. [A1, F1, F7, F9, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.4, algebra]

3.1 The test interpolation error in convection vanishes: continuity from [F11] bounds its integral by $C\|\Pi_jv-v\|_V\|\overline u_j\|_{L^2V}^2\|\eta\|_\infty$. The uniform left-endpoint test approximation from step 2.2 permits replacing the discrete weights by $\eta$. For fixed $v\in V_\sigma$, strong $L^2L^2$ convergence and the uniform $L^2L^6$ bound imply strong $L^2L^3$ and strong $L^2L^4$ convergence of velocities by Holder interpolation. In the skew formula, $u_j\otimes v$ then converges strongly in $L^2L^2$ while $\nabla u_j$ converges weakly in $L^2L^2$; $u_j\otimes u_j$ converges strongly in $L^1L^2$. Thus the convective term passes to $c(u;u,v)$. This proves the limiting momentum equation for all solenoidal tests. [F2, F3, F5, F11, step 1.4, step 2.2]

4.1 By [F14], $L^2(D)^d$ is separable, so balls with centers in a countable dense set and positive rational radii form a countable base. The space $H_\sigma=\overline{V_\sigma}^{L^2}$ from [F12] is a closed subspace and hence Hilbert by [F14]; intersecting that countable base with $H_\sigma$ gives a countable base there, and [A1] selects one point from each nonempty member to make a dense set. For every $v\in V_\sigma$, steps 2.2 and 3.1 give the scalar weak equation with $h_v(t)=(f(t),v)_{L^2}-a_\nu(u(t),v)-c(u(t);u(t),v)$. This function is integrable: its three terms lie in $L^2(0,T)$, $L^2(0,T)$, and $L^{4/3}(0,T)$ respectively by the data, energy bound [F1], and convection bound [F11]; finite $T$ embeds these spaces into $L^1$. The uniform $L^\infty H$ bound follows from step 1.4. Apply [F15] with $H=H_\sigma$ and $X=V_\sigma$ to obtain a unique weakly continuous representative with initial value $u_0$. Its energy inequality is already proved in step 2.3. [A1, F1, F11, F12, F14, F15, step 1.4, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1]

5.1 Steps 1.4, 2.1–2.3, 3.1, and 4.1 give the strong and weak convergence, divergence constraint, solenoidal momentum equation, weakly continuous initial trace, and energy inequality required by [[def-na-solenoidal-energy-weak-ns-velocity]]. The stronger pressure-bearing PE06 claim is not inferred here and remains escalated as stated. [step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

On each mesh take $u_j^0=P_{Z_j}u_0$, the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto the weak MINI kernel, and choose any backward Euler MINI solution from [[thm-na-mini-be-step-existence-energy]]. It does not assert the pressure regularity and pressure-bearing formulation required by the PE06 plan; the remaining pressure obligation is explicitly escalated on the A page.

The best-approximation property [F4] gives $\|P_{Z_j}u_0-u_0\|_2\le\|\Pi_jv-u_0\|_2\le\|\Pi_jv-v\|_2+\epsilon$. Letting $j\to\infty$ and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$ proves strong convergence of the discrete initial data. [A1, F3, F4, given, choose]

1.2 Apply [F1] to every mesh and partition. The energy inequality gives uniform bounds for $\max_n\|u_j^n\|_2$ and $\|\overline u_j\|_{L^2V}$; it also gives $\|\overline u_j\|_{L^\infty H}\le M$. [F1, given]

1.3 Fix a finite orthonormal family $e_1,\ldots,e_m\in V_\sigma$. For each mesh, $\Pi_je_i\in Z_j$ by [F3], so testing the discrete equation [F13] with $\Pi_je_i$ removes pressure. The backward difference of $a_{j,i}^n=(u_j^n,\Pi_je_i)_2$ is therefore bounded by $|(D_\tau a_{j,i}^n)|\le C_{e_i}\big(\|f_j^n\|_2+\nu\|u_j^n\|_V+\|u_j^n\|_2^{1/2}\|u_j^n\|_V^{3/2}\big).$ The first two terms are bounded in $L^2(0,T)$ by [F1], and the last in $L^{4/3}(0,T)$ by [F11], because its $4/3$ power is at most $M^{2/3}C\|u_j^n\|_V^2$. 4.1 By [F14], $L^2(D)^d$ is separable, so balls with centers in a countable dense set and positive rational radii form a countable base. 5.1 Steps 1.4, 2.1–2.3, 3.1, and 4.1 give the strong and weak convergence, divergence constraint, solenoidal momentum equation, weakly continuous initial trace, and energy inequality required by [[def-na-solenoidal-energy-weak-ns-velocity]]. The stronger pressure-bearing PE06 claim is not inferred here and remains escalated as stated. [step 1.4, step 2.1, step 2.2, step 2.3, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎
